findings.explanation: BSID-ZFBDT is the baseline date for due-date calculation, not the due date. The net due date is ZFBDT + ZBD3T (or ZBD1T/ZBD2T when only discount terms apply), exposed as NETDT in SAP's AR extractors. Using ZFBDT as the due date overstates days overdue by the full payment-term length. detailedImplementation Step 1 projects ZFBDT the same way.
findings.quote: due clock inputs `due_date`, SAP baseline `ZFBDT`, Oracle `due_date`, NetSuite `duedate`
findings.suggested_fix: Have the SQL view compute the net due date (ZFBDT + ZBD3T/ZBD2T/ZBD1T, or call DETERMINE_DUE_DATE / use the NETDT field of 0FI_AR_4-style extractors) and emit it as `due_date`. Describe ZFBDT only as the baseline.

findings.explanation: The `?` checkpoint placeholder and rising column apply to `mode = rising`. Batch mode re-imports the full result set on every run and keeps no checkpoint. DB Connect inputs are configured in db_inputs.conf, not inputs.conf, and 'Splunk lookahead macros' is not a DB Connect concept.
findings.quote: Emit hourly batch pulls matching representative inputs.conf semantics: `interval = 3600`, `mode = batch`, query predicates such as `WHERE last_updated > ?` using Splunk lookahead macros.
findings.suggested_fix: Either use `mode = rising` with `tail_rising_column_name = last_updated` and `WHERE last_updated > ?`, or use `mode = batch` as an explicit full open-item snapshot with a `snapshot_timestamp` column. Then say the SPL must take only the latest snapshot (see SPL flag).

findings.explanation: The SPL contains no mixed-currency warning. `eventstats sum(total_outstanding)` adds balances across `curr` values, so `pct_of_total` and `dso_days` become meaningless for multi-currency portfolios.
findings.quote: emits rolled balances suitable for mixed-currency portfolios only after upstream SQL translates into functional currency; Splunk warns when raw rows carry mixed currencies without normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the claim that Splunk warns. State that the SQL must emit a single reporting currency, or that `pct_of_total` and DSO must be computed per `curr`.

findings.explanation: BSID `DMBTR`/`WRBTR` are unsigned amounts; direction comes from `SHKZG`. Payments on account and credit memos in BSID would be added as positive receivables unless the SQL applies the sign. BSID is also already open-items-only, so the AUGDT filter is redundant, and on S/4HANA it is a compatibility view over ACDOCA/BSEG.
findings.quote: exposing open FI-AR analogues to **BSID** (`BUKRS`, `KUNNR`, `UMSKS`, `DMBTR`, `WRBTR`, `WAERS`, `ZFBDT`, `BUDAT`) filtered `AUGDT IS NULL`
findings.suggested_fix: Add `SHKZG` to the projection and emit a signed amount (e.g. `CASE SHKZG WHEN 'H' THEN -DMBTR ELSE DMBTR END`). Note that S/4HANA customers may prefer the ACDOCA-based CDS views.

findings.explanation: The SPL rolls up to aging_bucket × cust_segment × curr, so `cust_key`, per-invoice `days_overdue` and `ecl_amt` are not in its output. The grandmaExplanation's 'highlight who owes the most' also needs a per-customer view the search does not produce.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the drill table is a separate search (same evals, then `stats max(days_overdue) sum(amt_fc) sum(ecl_amt) by cust_key curr`).

findings.explanation: Asterisk (a VoIP PBX) and Microsoft 365 have nothing to do with AR aging from ERP subledgers, so they pollute equipment-based discovery.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `db_connect`, `sap`, `oracle` (and add NetSuite/Dynamics if mapped). Remove `asterisk` and `m365`.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by an authoring agent with no SME sign-off, and the due-date and ingestion errors above would not survive a finance SME review.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until a controller/treasury SME validates the SQL view and the totals against FBL5N.

findings.explanation: The reference title names a specific ASU, but the URL is the FASB home page.
findings.quote: "title": "FASB Accounting Standards Update ASU 2016-13 — Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments (CECL)", "url": "https://www.fasb.org/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the ASU 2016-13 / Topic 326 page on fasb.org directly.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search sums `amt_fc` over `earliest=-90d@d` of `dbx:ar_invoices` without keeping only the latest snapshot per invoice. With the documented hourly pulls of open items, each invoice is counted up to ~2,000 times, inflating `total_outstanding`, `portfolio_total` and `dso_days`. Restrict to the latest snapshot (e.g. `dedup invoice_key sortby -_time` or `where _time=latest_snapshot`) before `stats`.

`eventstats sum(total_outstanding) as portfolio_total` sums across all `curr` values, so `pct_of_total` and `dso_days` mix currencies whenever more than one currency is present. Compute these per `curr` or after FX normalization.

`coalesce(amount,amount_due_remaining,...)` prefers `amount` (often the original invoice amount) over `amount_due_remaining`, which overstates partially paid invoices. The enterprise ×1.15 / SMB ×0.85 ECL multipliers are also counter-intuitive and undocumented.

summary: This is one of the better-grounded UCs in the subcategory: the aging, ECL and DSO logic is explained clearly and the troubleshooting is practical. However, it treats SAP `ZFBDT` (the baseline date) as the due date, describes an hourly batch input with a rising-mode `?` checkpoint, and aggregates 90 days of repeated open-item snapshots without deduplication, so balances will be badly inflated.
